issues.description: Fixed-size packetization lacks real-time pacing despite claiming to provide it
issues.detail: The PR description and the new `fixed_audio_packet_size` docstring promise 'real-time pacing' for media endpoints like Vonage Audio Connector, but the implementation only does fixed-size chunking. `_write_frame` immediately flushes every full chunk via `_client.send` in a tight `while` loop without consulting `_send_interval` or `_next_send_time`. The invariant 'one fixed-size packet is emitted per packet-duration' is not maintained; bursts of large payloads will be sent back-to-back. Either pace the sends against `_next_send_time` (which already exists in the class) or remove the 'real-time pacing' claim from the docstring/changelog.

issues.description: Loop invariant for packetization buffer is not stated and silently drops trailing audio on shutdown
issues.detail: The new send-buffer code has an implicit invariant ('after each call, `len(_audio_send_buffer) < packet_bytes`') that is not documented and not enforced at session end. Any remainder smaller than `packet_bytes` is held indefinitely and never flushed (e.g., on EndFrame / disconnect), so the tail of the final utterance is silently truncated. Knuth's rule: state the invariant in a comment, and handle the termination case explicitly (flush with zero-padding to `packet_bytes`, or document that trailing < packet_bytes audio is discarded by design).

issues.description: Packetization path unconditionally treats every bytes payload as audio
issues.detail: `_write_frame` checks `isinstance(payload, (bytes, bytearray))` to decide whether to apply `fixed_audio_packet_size` chunking. But any serializer is free to return `bytes` for non-audio frames (control messages, binary protocol frames, future frame types). Splitting a non-audio binary payload at an audio-frame boundary will corrupt it. The intended invariant is 'this buffer contains only PCM samples of the configured width'; enforce it by gating on the source frame type (`isinstance(frame, AudioRawFrame)`) rather than on payload type, or by having the serializer tag audio output explicitly.

issues.description: `fixed_audio_packet_size` is in bytes but has no validation against frame/sample-width alignment
issues.detail: The parameter is documented as '640 for 20ms @ 16kHz PCM16 mono' but nothing checks that the buffered bytes split cleanly on sample boundaries. If a user sets, say, 641, or the upstream resampler emits an odd byte count, the chunk boundaries will fall mid-sample and produce garbled audio downstream. Either validate `packet_bytes % sample_width == 0` at setup, or express the parameter in samples/milliseconds and compute bytes internally. State the alignment invariant explicitly.

issues.description: `bytes(self._audio_send_buffer[:packet_bytes])` allocates O(n) per chunk; consider memoryview
issues.detail: Each iteration of the send loop slices the bytearray, allocates a new immutable bytes object, then `del`s the prefix, which shifts the remainder of the buffer in memory. Asymptotically this is fine for small `packet_bytes` (~640 B), but a `collections.deque` of fixed-size frames or a `memoryview` + index pointer with periodic compaction would avoid the O(n) shift on every packet. Not the hot spot today (Knuth: don't optimize without measuring), but worth a literate comment acknowledging the choice if it is intentional.

`json.dumps(frame.message)` assumes `frame.message` is JSON-serializable. There is no try/except around it, and no contract documented in the docstring. A non-JSON-able payload will raise `TypeError` out of `serialize`, which `_write_frame` only catches as a generic exception and logs. State the precondition ('message must be JSON-serializable') in the docstring, or wrap and log with a more specific message.

issues.description: DTMF parsing accepts two undocumented Vonage payload shapes without source citation
issues.detail: The deserializer reads `message.get('digit') or message.get('dtmf', {}).get('digit')` with a comment 'Vonage may send digit in different formats, try both'. There is no link to the Vonage docs section that specifies the two shapes, no test fixture for either, and no preference order rationale. This is exactly the kind of non-obvious code that wants a literate-programming comment with a doc URL anchored to the relevant section, plus at least one unit test per shape so a future reader can verify the assumption.

issues.description: No tests accompany the new serializer or the packetization buffer
issues.detail: There are no unit tests for `VonageFrameSerializer.serialize`/`deserialize` (audio resample path, DTMF parsing, JSON dispatch, clear/notify events) and no tests for the new `fixed_audio_packet_size` buffering in `FastAPIWebsocketTransport` (boundary alignment, interruption-clears-buffer, payload-smaller-than-packet, payload-larger-than-2x-packet). Knuth: proofs catch what tests miss and tests catch what proofs miss. Without either, the packetization invariant rests on inspection alone.

review.summary: The change is small and the algorithm is straightforward, but it is UNDER-AUDITED in the Knuth sense: the new packetization buffer has an unstated loop invariant, no termination handling for trailing bytes at session end, no alignment guard against sample-width mismatches, and no pacing despite the PR claiming 'real-time pacing.' The `isinstance(payload, bytes)` gate also conflates 'binary' with 'audio,' which will silently corrupt any non-audio binary payload a future serializer emits. The Vonage serializer itself is clean and readable, but the dual-shape DTMF parsing and the JSON-dispatch table both want a literate comment with a doc citation, and the whole PR ships without unit tests for either the new serializer or the new buffering path. NEEDS-LITERATE-COMMENT on the buffer; UNDER-AUDITED overall; not blocking on asymptotics (the chunking is O(total bytes) amortized and the constants are fine at 640 B), so the bytearray-slice cost is a deliberate non-optimization rather than a defect.
